summary: Inspect a bounded rigid robot approach/contact/hold/retreat task whose controller, collision solver and state transitions have separate authority.
objective: Build a contact-task viewer where an external dynamics solver advances a rigid arm under a declared controller and reports contact forces without treating kinematic overlap as contact evidence.
example_prompts: Move a rigid end effector toward a plane, enter contact on solver evidence, regulate a target normal force, then retreat.
negative_signals: Not a safety-certified controller, real robot calibration, grasp planner or collision-free guarantee.
not_for: No flexible links, actuator electronics, tactile estimation, human contact, learned policy or real-time guarantee.

entities.name: Robot and collision proxies
entities.guidance: Blender authors link shells, named joint/tool frames and simple collision proxies as separate nodes; visual meshes never serve as unreviewed solver shapes.

entities.name: Task/controller/contact panel
entities.guidance: Three.js orchestrates immutable requests and renders solver-returned q, qdot, actuator input, contact IDs, normal force and residual by generation.

state_contract.model: Use a finite rigid articulated model in an external dynamics engine with positive masses/inertias, declared joints, collision proxies, timestep and solver settings. Task phases are idle, approach, contact-hold, retreat, complete, error. A controller produces bounded actuator input from the current solver state and target; only the dynamics engine integrates dynamic bodies. A kinematic target may move as a reference but cannot be interpreted as exerting force unless the solver reports a contact constraint and force for the exact step. Enter contact-hold only after an allowed proxy pair reports contact with finite normal force; leave on separation, force-limit violation, stale generation, solver error or cancel. Reset restores q/qdot/controller state/contact set/phase and invalidates pending results.
state_contract.authority: The external rigid-body/contact engine owns integration, constraints and contact forces. Application controller owns task targets, phase and limits. Three.js owns adapter generations, history and presentation; Blender owns link/tool/collision construction.
actions: Start approach from a validated home state.
Change target pose or normal-force target and create a new generation.
Retreat or reset and confirm contact/controller state clears.

invariants: Dynamic link poses come only from accepted solver output; kinematic targets are references.
Contact phase requires an allowed solver contact ID and finite force from the current generation.
Actuator and force limits reject/terminate the step without being hidden by animation.
A late result after cancel/reset/new request is discarded.
motion_guidance: Play, pause and step advance the declared model clock only; reset restores parameters, state, solver budget, selections, errors and presentation transforms.
Use static before/after states and numeric tables for reduced motion; animation interpolates committed state and never supplies physical evidence.
creative_affordances: Blender may shape distinctive apparatus, cutaways and materials; Three.js binds named parts to authoritative state and keeps units and error states readable.
Camera, color, trails and deformation gain are presentation controls and cannot change the numerical model.
known_limits: Pedagogical external-solver adapter only; controller gains, collision proxies and soft-contact parameters are authored fixture inputs, not safe real-robot settings.
Authored, source-reviewed guidance only; no Blender export, numerical simulation, contact solve, browser or renderer was run.

claims.statement: MuJoCo documents soft constraints in which impedance, stiffness and damping control constraint response through solver parameters such as solref and solimp.
claims.scope: MuJoCo stable documentation read 2026-09-08; backend-specific behavior requiring installed-version verification.

source_refs.locator: Solver parameters: impedance, stiffness, damping, solref and solimp

claims.statement: MuJoCo documents semi-implicit Euler as updating position with the new velocity and provides multiple integrators; timestep and integrator are therefore explicit simulation inputs rather than animation timing.
claims.scope: MuJoCo stable computation documentation; no stability guarantee for this authored task.

source_refs.locator: Numerical Integration, equations 2–3 and integrator discussion

object_craft.structure: Build named joint and tool-frame empties, low-complexity collision proxies and a target fixture; keep proxy visibility toggleable beside render shells.
object_craft.material: Use phase text and force arrows with numeric units; contact glow appears only from current solver contact data.

physical_contract.scope: External rigid articulated dynamics and soft contact under a bounded application controller/task state machine.
physical_contract.timestep: Pinned engine timestep/integrator/solver settings; accept outputs only for the current immutable generation.
contact: external engine contact constraints and reported forces
